messages:
maria: Heads-up: ran into a reproducible hang when streaming with the Python SDK sample. Repro is async httpx against our SSE endpoint. After a 401-triggered token refresh the async generator stops yielding the final chunk and caller cancel just blocks.

maria: stripped repro:
```py
async def stream_events(client):
    async with client.stream('GET', '/v1/events', headers={'Authorization': token}) as r:
        async for chunk in r.aiter_text():
            yield chunk
```

maria: behavior: works until mid-stream 401 -> refresh -> subsequent reads never finish, no exception, socket remains ESTABLISHED. consumer cancelling task hangs.

alex: which httpx/uvloop/python? sounds like an aclose/finalizer ordering edge.

maria: httpx 0.24.0, py3.11, uvloop. running inside a FastAPI test harness hitting hosted endpoint returning chunked SSE.

devon: are you relying on generator finalizers for cleanup? that can race with cancellation.

maria: yes, caller does a simple async for and breaks on a condition, not explicitly closing the response. adding try/finally with explicit await r.aclose() fixes locally.

sam: thats consistent with the old socket-leak race. We added abort() on one path previously. For SDK we should provide an explicit abort/aclose on the iterator and docs showing async-with usage.

alex: agree. Short-term we should: document correct pattern and give an explicit API (stream.abort/aclose). Mid-term: surface a StreamAuthError if a 401 happens while streaming so callers can react, instead of silently hanging.

jiao: filing two items: docs+example for 'async with' streaming and a typed wrapper class to help mypy users. Many folks see typing noise when using AsyncIterator[str] vs Iterator[bytes].

maria: opened a quick GH repro (link omitted). Two patch ideas: (A) Surface StreamAuthError into iterator on 401 during streaming. (B) Try transparent resume by replaying prefix cache from server if supported. Option B requires server-side support, so risky.

devon: option A seems straightforward. We should guarantee iterator either yields final chunk or raises a clear exception. Also ensure abort/idempotent close closes the socket immediately.

sam: I'll draft the StreamAuthError and abort API. Proposal: stream = client.stream(...); async with stream: async for t in stream: ... ; + stream.abort() that is idempotent and ensures underlying transport closed. Add unit test simulating 401 mid-stream expecting StreamAuthError.

alex: plus add typed helper: class Stream[str]: implements AsyncIterator[str] and AsyncContextManager, so mypy is happy and docs can show correct annotations. Example snippet in quickstart.

jiao: i'll open PRs for docs and typing wrapper. sam, can you open the SDK PR for the error type and abort API? assign to eng-runtime.

sam: yep. Also note: the sample app had a retry middleware that retried on 401 which made the socket linger. removed the middleware and behavior is reproducible without retries.

ci-bot: auto-note: issue created devex#4582 stream-auth-hang by jiao.

alex: plan: 1) docs patch to quickstart and streaming guide (show async with + abort), 2) SDK change to raise StreamAuthError on 401 mid-stream, 3) typing wrapper + examples, 4) consider resume_on_reauth opt-in feature later. Add to py-sdk 0.25 milestone.

maria: thanks y'all, docs workaround unblocks my demo tomorrow. :relieved:
